record.paper_title: Relativistic jets in narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
record.context_brief: comparison with blazars and radio galaxies
record.original_question: Gamma-ray-emitting narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies are active galactic nuclei with relativistic jets, but the previously established gamma-ray jet populations were blazars and radio galaxies. What are the differences between gamma-ray-emitting narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies and blazars or radio galaxies in their physical properties, jet behavior, or evolutionary status?

evidence.quote: What are the differences between this class of γ-ray emitting AGNs and blazars and radio galaxies?

artifact.category_tag: Active galactic nuclei and relativistic jets
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent multiwavelength studies have made substantial progress: gamma-ray NLS1s are now generally interpreted as low-black-hole-mass, high-accretion-rate, possibly "young" analogues of flat-spectrum radio quasars, with evidence (sometimes contested) that some are hosted in spiral rather than elliptical galaxies, and with jet powers consistent with the nonlinear scaling of jet power with black-hole mass. However, central questions—host morphology of the most luminous γ-NLS1s, true black-hole mass distribution, and whether they form a genuinely distinct population or an evolutionary phase of blazars—remain actively debated, so the problem is only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Relativistic Jets in Gamma-Ray-Emitting Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 Galaxies (MDPI, 2019)
status_evidence.snippet: γ-NLSy1 galaxies are an enigmatic member of RL-AGNs... could be hosted by spiral galaxies, making them different from blazars hosted by elliptical galaxies; may be a low-luminosity, low-BH-mass counterpart of FSRQs.
status_evidence.claim: Substantial progress identifying γ-NLS1s as a distinct/low-mass counterpart of FSRQs, but key questions remain.

status_evidence.title: Gamma-ray Emitting Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 Galaxies: Past, Present, and Future (arXiv:1909.01444)
status_evidence.snippet: Review of γ-NLS1s ten years after their discovery, discussing open questions on jet power, black hole mass, host galaxy and evolutionary status.
status_evidence.claim: Open questions on host, mass, and evolution of γ-NLS1s persist as of 2019 review.

status_evidence.title: Gamma-Ray-emitting NLS1 in SDSS (ApJL, 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: New γ-NLS1 detections used to characterize physical properties of relativistic jets at different accretion and mass scales.
status_evidence.claim: Active observational program continues to refine the comparison with blazars.
